problem: Analytics measured that the local goal planner had succeeded 0 times out of 18 in seven days while the cloud planner was 77 of 77, so ARIES was silently planning in the cloud while presenting itself as local-first, at a cost of 1,397,433 input tokens over 77 calls. Every local call returned HTTP 503 with the body 'Local inference failed: HTTPStatusError' and no further detail.
change: Reproduced the failure directly against the gateway, then isolated it: the same request with a trivial schema returned 200, so the generated planner schema was the cause. Bisected the schema field by field, then keyword by keyword, against the live runtime. An unbounded string is refused, as are title, pattern, and a maxLength large enough to blow up the grammar expansion; maxLength 80, minLength+maxLength, integer with or without bounds, boolean, enum and array-of-string are all accepted. The planner schema carried reason and summary as bare strings plus a value at maxLength 2000 and an expected_sha256 with a pattern. Added grammar_safe() to aries/workspace/agent_planner.py, which keeps only type, enum, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength and items and bounds every string at 512, and applied it to every generated field and to the prose fields.
validation: The identical request that returned 503 now returns 200 against the live gateway. Schema size 5,417 to 4,236 characters. All 58 allowed capabilities are still offered in the enum and the action verbs still narrow correctly when finish and fail are withheld. tests/test_planner_grammar.py holds the measured shape statically so a capability added later with a pattern or an unbounded string cannot take local planning down silently; 20 checks pass. Six planner-touching suites re-run green: agent_execution, operator, workspace, intelligence, goal_planner, coding. The measurement table for every keyword tested is recorded in the module comment and in docs/ERROR_LOG.md entry 028.
limitations: The blocker is removed; plan quality is not fixed. A local plan now returns but the content is poor, one test goal producing arguments.task_id and a runaway mode string rather than naming a capability, and the system prompt does not currently tell the model that capability must be one of the enum values. Dropping constraints from the grammar means a malformed argument is caught one step later, by the per-capability validator, at the cost of a retry. Only the ollama backend was measured; the openai-compatible local backend was not. It is not established whether the 18 recorded failures predate the four capability modules added the same day, so the schema may have been unusable for longer than the seven-day window shows. A test walker I wrote first flagged the field names title and pattern as schema keywords, which is a false positive worth remembering: notification.send has a field called title and system.services one called pattern.
